# Git `--max-count-oldest` without the `--reverse` Trap

## Thesis

People often want the **oldest N commits** of a range. The folklore `git log --reverse | head` is fragile. Newer Git adds **`--max-count-oldest`** (Git **2.55+**). This box has Git **2.47.3**, so the new flag is documented as **not run** locally.

## Mental model

```text
  good (Git ≥ 2.55): git log --max-count-oldest=5 main..HEAD
  fragile: git log --reverse main..feature | head -5
```

## Worked examples

```bash
git --version
git log -h 2>&1 | grep max-count-oldest || echo "flag not in this git"
```

On this host: `git version 2.47.3` — flag not present.

## Trap

**`--reverse | head` in scripts.** Buffering and full walks make it a bad automation default.

## Boring rule

Document the minimum Git version next to any script that uses `--max-count-oldest`.

## Try this

1. On Git 2.55+, compare timings on a long branch.
2. Read the Git 2.55 release notes.
3. Add a CI check for minimum `git` version.

## Sources

- Git 2.55 release notes / `git-log(1)`
